sections.html:
Porter County fills the northwest corner of Indiana, with Lake Michigan on its northern edge and the Kankakee River to the south. Valparaiso is the county seat. Portage, the largest city by population and land area, is the other city, and 173,215 people lived in the county at the 2020 census. Nine towns fill in the map: Beverly Shores, Burns Harbor, Chesterton, Dune Acres, Hebron, Kouts, Ogden Dunes, Porter and Town of Pines. Twelve townships carry the assessment work: Boone, Center, Jackson, Liberty, Morgan, Pine, Pleasant, Portage, Porter, Union, Washington and Westchester.

Because a parcel can sit in a city, a town, a township only or a lakeshore community, each with its own levy mix, tax statements for a lake-side house in Ogden Dunes and a farmhouse near Kouts can look very different even though both go to the same county treasurer.

Three county offices share the work. Read the TS-1A that comes with your bill first, then sort the question using the table.

QuestionOfficeContact
Assessment went upAssessor, 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 211, Valparaiso(219) 465-3460
A deduction dropped offAuditor(219) 465-3445; Auditor@porterco.org
Payment posted wrongTreasurer, 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso(219) 465-3470

The tax rate itself is set at the state level, so none of the three offices can change it. If you are selling, the Auditor is also where you confirm that a homestead deduction is on file, since a buyer's lender will look at the same record.

Bills come in two installments. Spring is due May 10 and fall is due November 10, and a date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Any bill under $25.00 is not split. The county accepts full and partial payments all year, and late amounts carry penalties.

A payment counts as on time when the properly addressed envelope has a U.S. postmark on or before the due date, or when an express carrier delivered it by then. The county points to Indiana Code 6-1.1-37-10 for the penalty rules, and the calculation is printed on the front of the bill.

  • Online through the county's two payment portals: electronic checks carry no extra charge and cards carry a processing fee.
  • By phone or mail, using the instructions on the county's payment pages. Mail goes to the Treasurer at 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso, IN 46383, and the check should not be stapled to the coupon.
  • In person at the Treasurer's office.
  • Through a mortgage, escrow or title company, each of which has its own electronic portfolio system.

An online payment needs at least two days to post, so the lookup page can still show a balance for a bit. Account history updates nightly. Surplus claim forms go out after the June and December settlements if you overpay, and a spring overpayment is applied to the fall amount.

Delinquent parcels can end up in an online auction on zeusauction.com. To pull a property from the sale, the Treasurer must receive cash or certified funds at 155 Indiana Avenue, Suite 209 before the cutoff stated in that year's notice, which falls the day before the sale opens.

An owner whose property sells can still redeem it. Redemption costs 110 percent of the minimum bid within six months of the sale and 115 percent after that, plus any overbid with 5 percent annual interest on it, plus later taxes the buyer paid. For certificates sold in the 2026 sale, the redemption period runs to Friday, October 22, 2027. If a property sells above the minimum bid and is not redeemed, the former owner of record may be entitled to the surplus.

Some taxpayers qualify for a tax sale payment plan, and a property that is not sold but is pursued for title carries a 120 day redemption window. Redemption questions go to the Auditor at (219) 465-3449, and payment plan questions to the Treasurer at taxquestions@porterco.org.

Begin with Form 130, filed with the assessing official. Where no township assessor exists, that is the county Assessor. File one form per parcel. For a current-year assessment the form is due June 15 of the assessment year if the notice was mailed before May 1, and June 15 of the year tax statements go out if it was mailed on or after May 1.

A separate, limited error correction route lets you file within three years after the taxes were first due. Evidence is not required at filing, but both sides swap what they have at a preliminary informal meeting.

  • If the meeting fails, the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals must hold a hearing within 180 days of filing, with at least 30 days of notice to you.
  • You may then take the result to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131 within 45 days.
  • The last stop is the Indiana Tax Court, again within 45 days of the board's final decision.

Indiana limits what an owner pays as a share of gross assessed value: 1 percent for a homestead with the standard deduction, 2 percent for other residential property and agricultural land, and 3 percent for nonresidential and personal property. When the calculated tax runs above the cap, the difference comes off the bill as a circuit breaker credit.

The 2025 reform known as SEA 1 is reshaping the deductions. The $48,000 standard deduction steps down each year after 2026, the supplemental deduction rises, and a new homestead credit of 10 percent of the bill, up to $300, begins in 2026. The effect varies with home value, so read your own statement before you tell a buyer what the taxes will be.

sections.h2: Selling a Porter County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Start by getting the parcel's balance from the Treasurer, then decide how it will be paid at closing. A title company wants unpaid taxes settled at closing, and a property already on the certified list needs the redemption amount rather than the base tax.

  • Pull the bill and the lookup balance, and check whether a spring or fall installment is still open.
  • Ask the Auditor whether any deduction on the parcel will lapse after the sale.
  • If the house is on the tax sale list, ask about the redemption figure and the payment plan.
  • Tell the title company about any open appeal.

With two installments a year, a sale between due dates can leave one open, so ask the title company how that amount will be split at closing. Homes near the lakefront or the South Shore Line stations often draw different buyers than rural homes in the south, which affects how fast a house moves and what condition problems buyers will accept.

A cash sale can close around a tax problem. The title company pays the balance or redemption amount out of your proceeds, so you do not have to find the money first. It also skips the lender's appraisal, so a house with repair needs is judged on its condition and not held up for a loan.

faqs.q: What are the Porter County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Spring is due May 10 and fall is due November 10. A weekend or holiday moves either date to the next business day, and a postmark on or before the date counts as on time.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Porter County tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it with the coupon to the Treasurer at 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso, IN 46383. Do not staple or clip the check to the coupon, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for a receipt in about six to eight weeks.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a higher assessment in Porter County?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at (219) 465-3460. Call the Auditor at (219) 465-3445 if a deduction dropped, and the Treasurer at (219) 465-3470 if a payment posted wrong.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Porter County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes, but the delinquent taxes and costs have to be cleared before the sale or redeemed afterward. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff and the Auditor for the redemption amount, and have the title company put it on the closing statement.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an assessment in Porter County?
faqs.a: For a current-year assessment, Form 130 is generally due by June 15, depending on when the notice was mailed. A limited error correction can be filed within three years after the taxes were first due.
